findings.summary: The new port is unwired. link.rs (and everything above it) still parses and builds frames with the external `mavlink` crate 0.21 (`use mavlink::dialects::ardupilotmega::*`, MavlinkReader, write_versioned_msg). Nothing outside extlibs/mavlink references MavlinkParse, MAVLinkMessage, MAVLinkParam, MAVLinkParamList or dotnet.rs (grep confirms). The crate is built from its own bundled XML, not ExtLibs/Mavlink/message_definitions + offspec.xml. It does not implement the fork's MAVLINK_IFLAG_SYSID32/TARGET32 wide headers (MavlinkHeader.cs), so the running app cannot speak Mission Planner's wire protocol.
findings.required_fix: Port MAVLinkInterface.cs/MAVState.cs/MAVList.cs onto extlibs::mavlink, switch link.rs consumers over, and remove the `mavlink` crate dependency.

findings.summary: The progress metric is inflated about 24x. classify() returns 'generated' for Mavlink.cs, but lines 174-176 then turn any file with a header into 'ported', which moves Mavlink.cs into the owned/ported totals. MANIFEST.md therefore reports 40,678/473,584 ported lines instead of 1,646/434,552. The 7 pymavlink/generator/CS/*.cs template copies (1,419 lines) are also counted as owned 'todo' although copy_fixed_headers ships them as the same files as ExtLibs/Mavlink/*.cs.
findings.required_fix: Keep 'generated'/'vendored'/'n/a' sticky: report header presence for those rows separately and exclude them from owned totals. Class pymavlink/generator/CS/*.cs as generated copies.

findings.summary: INT8 SetValue writes different bytes. C# `BitConverter.GetBytes((sbyte)input)` binds to GetBytes(short) because there is no sbyte overload, so -1 becomes [FF FF 00 00]. Rust writes [FF 00 00 00]. Value/int8_value agree, but `data` and `float_value` differ. MAVLinkInterface.setParam sends `new MAVLinkParam(...).float_value` for non-ArduPilot autopilots, so the wire bits would differ. No test covers negative INT8.
findings.required_fix: Encode INT8 as `(cast_i8(input) as i16).to_le_bytes()` resized to 4 and add a test asserting [0xFF,0xFF,0,0] for -1.

findings.summary: All ReaderWriterLock semantics are dropped: the 1000 ms acquire timeouts, the ApplicationException on timeout, reentrant writer locking in Add->indexer, and reader locks in ContainsKey and the Dictionary conversion. The justification ('the owner MAVState holds the whole list behind its own lock') is false, because MAVState.cs is not ported and nothing owns this type.
findings.required_fix: Port the locker (e.g. parking_lot RwLock with try_*_for(1000ms) mapping to an ApplicationException variant) inside MAVLinkParamList, or port MAVState in the same round and prove the invariant.

findings.summary: The C# class is a List<MAVLinkParam>, so callers use the int indexer setter, Remove, RemoveAt, Insert, Sort, Find, FindIndex, ForEach and the base (non-`new`) Add/AddRange through IList. Rust exposes only an immutable Deref<Target=Vec>, so none of the mutating List members exist. PropertyChanged handlers receive only a &str (no sender or PropertyChangedEventArgs) and cannot be removed (-=).
findings.required_fix: Expose the List<T> surface (DerefMut or explicit methods with C#-matching names and semantics) and model the event with sender, args and unsubscribe.

findings.summary: In C#, MAVLINK_MESSAGE_INFOS is a mutable static field that MavlinkMessagePlugin replaces at runtime to add messages. In Rust it is an immutable `pub static &[message_info]` (generated), and get_message_info caches a HashMap index keyed on that exact pointer. A ported MavlinkMessagePlugin cannot extend the table, and a swapped table would bypass or desync the cache.
findings.required_fix: Make MAVLINK_MESSAGE_INFOS a replaceable RwLock<Arc<[message_info]>> (or similar) and invalidate the index on replacement.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Mavlink/MAVLinkMessage.cs:249; MAVLinkParam.cs:222-232; MainV2.cs:4234-4236 (CurrentCulture left at OS culture)
findings.summary: Culture is hard-coded. DateTime.ToString() is fixed to en-US 'M/d/yyyy h:mm:ss tt', and double/float ToString always use '.'. Mission Planner only sets CurrentUICulture (the CurrentCulture line is commented out), so on a de-DE or fr machine C# prints '08.11.2026 13:04:09' and '0,8'. MAVLinkMessage.ToString and MAVLinkParam.ToString/default_value_to_string diverge on every non-en-US system.
findings.required_fix: Add a CurrentCulture abstraction (decimal separator, date pattern) sourced from the OS locale and use it in all ToString shims.

findings.summary: to_local_time applies the current UTC offset (chrono::Local::now()) to any instant. .NET applies TimeZoneInfo.Local's adjustment rule for that instant. Tlog packet times recorded on the other side of a DST change come out one hour off.
findings.required_fix: Use chrono::Local.from_utc_datetime(instant).offset() for the specific timestamp, and to_universal_time likewise.

findings.summary: Three public C# types are not ported; they are folded into generated metadata (FieldInfo.units, EnumEntry.description, has_location). C# code that does `GetCustomAttributes(...).OfType<MAVLink.Units>()` or reads `Description.Text` through reflection on any type, not just MAVLink structs, has no counterpart. Units.Unit and Description.Text are also settable in C#.
findings.required_fix: Port the attribute classes as types (e.g. structs Units{unit}, Description{text}, hasLocation) and expose an attribute-query API that mirrors GetCustomAttributes.

findings.summary: StructureToByteArrayBigEndian differs from C# for sbyte fields and non-byte arrays. C#'s switch has no SByte case, so int8 fields are left 0, and `(byte[])fieldValue` throws InvalidCastException for float[]/ushort[]/sbyte[] arrays. Rust copies the sbyte value and silently serialises every array type. C# also accepts any object (`params object[]`); Rust only MarshalStruct.
findings.required_fix: Reproduce the C# behaviour: zero sbyte fields and return an InvalidCast error for non-byte arrays.

findings.summary: ByteArrayToStructureEndian: when the source is too short, C# catches the Marshal.Copy exception, logs 'ByteArrayToStructure FAIL' plus ex.ToString() to Console, and marshals uninitialised HGlobal memory. Rust silently zero-fills. ByteArrayToStructureGC(Type,...) at :113 clamps a short buffer instead of the C# Buffer.BlockCopy ArgumentException, and the 4-buffer SemaphoreSlim pool with its 'Failed to get free buffer' InvalidOperationException (:145-190) is absent.
findings.required_fix: Emit the same Console diagnostics and error paths, or document each as unreachable and add tests proving it.

findings.summary: message_info::EMPTY uses name "" where C# has null, and `type` is null in both. msgtypename for an unknown id returns "" where C# returns null, so a C# `msgtypename == null` check cannot be expressed. message_info fields are plain pub where C# has `internal set`.
findings.required_fix: Use Option<&'static str> for name, matching null.

findings.summary: Some behaviour is invented. MAVLinkMessage gets a deep Clone, MAVLinkParam derives Clone+PartialEq (value equality where C# compares references), and MAVLinkParamList gets Clone. None exist in C#; the PartialEq in particular changes semantics for code that compares params. MAVLinkParam.default_value is a mutable pub field where C# has `public readonly`. MAVLinkParam.data() returns an immutable &[u8;4], while the C# getter returns the live array and callers can mutate it in place.
findings.required_fix: Remove the invented derives (use Arc identity where C# shares references), make default_value read-only, and expose a mutable data accessor.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Mavlink/Mavlink.cs:8 (`MAVLINK_BUILD_DATE = "Sun Oct 04 2026"`); mavgen.py parse_time (time.strftime, local time)
findings.summary: MAVLINK_BUILD_DATE is regenerated on every build ('Sat Nov 07 2026' in the current OUT_DIR), so the constant differs from Mission Planner's shipped value. The date is computed in UTC, but mavgen uses local time.
findings.required_fix: Pin SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the reference build date, or emit the reference constant, and use local time when unpinned.

findings.summary: There are two latent generator divergences. An empty units="" attribute becomes "[]" in Rust but "" in mavparse. parse_value supports only decimal, hex and a**b, while mavparse eval()s any Python expression (e.g. 1<<3). Neither occurs in the current XML, so the output matches today.
findings.required_fix: Match `if units:` truthiness and support at least the shift and or-expressions eval accepts.

findings.cs_reference: pymavlink/generator/mavgen_cs.py:316-318 (enum comment only for non-array fields)
findings.summary: FieldInfo.enum_name and display are invented runtime metadata. C# exposes no enum or display information at runtime (only a /*ENUM*/ comment), and Rust also sets enum_name on array fields where C# has none (mavlink_trajectory_representation_waypoints_t.command). Anything built on enum_name will behave differently from the C# MAVLink inspector.
findings.required_fix: Drop enum_name/display from runtime metadata, or confine it to doc comments as C# does.

findings.summary: The tests are weak. The reference tests return early and pass when reference/ is absent, so they are vacuous in CI. every_enum_member_matches captures the underlying type but never asserts it, and never checks [Flags]/[Obsolete]/hasLocation/[Description]; this judge verified those separately. every_struct_field_matches ignores [Units]/[Description]. The signing test (mavlinkparse.rs:315-331) asserts only sig length 13, not SHA-256/48 bytes against a known C# vector. No test covers ReadWithTimeout's timeout path, the hasTimestamp path, MAVLinkMessage.ToString, or INT8 data bytes.
findings.required_fix: Fail (not skip) when reference is missing in CI, assert all attributes, and add golden byte vectors produced by the C# for signing, ToString and MAVLinkParam.data.

findings.cs_reference: .NET Framework 4.7.2 TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds/FromSeconds (Interval rounds to whole ms), DateTime.AddMilliseconds range check

verdict: This round adds a careful, mostly faithful transliteration of seven small hand-written ExtLibs/Mavlink files, plus a build.rs port of mavgen_cs. The generator output matches the reference Mavlink.cs in every message_info row (msgid, name, crc_extra, min length, length), every enum's underlying type, [Flags], [Obsolete], hasLocation and descriptions, and every struct field. That is good work, but it is under 0.4% of Mission Planner's owned code, and none of it is used: the running app still talks MAVLink through the third-party `mavlink` crate, which cannot handle the fork's wide-ID headers. The ported files still diverge in places: INT8 param bytes, dropped ReaderWriterLock semantics, missing List<T> members and attribute classes, an immutable message table, culture- and DST-blind formatting, and invented Clone/PartialEq. The manifest also overstates progress about 24x by counting generated Mavlink.cs as ported. The pre-manifest egui app has broad feature coverage across FlightData, FlightPlanner and config pages, but it is a reimplementation, not an exact clone. Overall 0.8/10 (cap 1.1); round-file fidelity 6.5/10.
